composition.story: The heart is two pumps side by side. Step through one heartbeat: the atria fill and top up the ventricles, then the ventricles squeeze. Watch the four valves. Inlet valves slam shut before outlet valves open, so the squeeze can only push blood forward: 70 mL to the lungs and 70 mL to the body.

aha.observation: During ejection, the inlet valves are shut and the outlet valves are open. Both ventricles push the same 70 mL forward, at 120 mmHg on the left and 25 mmHg on the right.

parts.presentation: Five heartbeat steps above the picture; active step highlighted
Trace inside the rail showing steps already visited
Fixed four-chamber heart: right side on the viewer's left, vessels at top, flow arrows as links, active chambers and valves highlighted
Faint outline of the previous step's highlighted regions
Anchored to the key valve or chamber; shows location, no numbers duplicated from readouts
Readout strip below the picture: volumes in mL, pressures in mmHg, rounded to 5

controls.label: Heartbeat step
controls.presentation: Previous and Next buttons, keyboard arrows; names kept when disabled at the first or last step

variants.label: Resting adult heart (~70 beats/min, typical textbook values, rounded to 5)

states.label: Atria fill
states.sentence: Veins fill both atria. The open tricuspid and mitral valves let blood drain passively into the relaxed ventricles.
states.why: Ventricle pressure is below atrial pressure, so the inlet valves stay open and the outlet valves stay shut.

states.label: Atria squeeze
states.sentence: Both atria contract together and push a final top-up into the ventricles before the ventricles squeeze.
states.why: This atrial kick adds about 10 mL, so each ventricle is full before contraction.

states.label: Inlet valves shut (lub)
states.sentence: The ventricles start squeezing. Rising pressure slams the tricuspid and mitral valves shut, making the first heart sound, lub.
states.why: All four valves are closed, so volume holds steady while pressure climbs toward artery pressure.

states.label: Ventricles eject
states.sentence: Ventricle pressure beats artery pressure, so the outlet valves open. Blood leaves: the right side to the lungs, the left side to the body.
states.why: Closed inlet valves block backflow, so the squeeze can only push blood forward through the outlets.

states.label: Outlet valves shut (dub)
states.sentence: The ventricles relax. Blood in the arteries pushes back and snaps the pulmonary and aortic valves shut, making the second sound, dub.
states.why: With all valves closed again, pressure falls until the inlet valves reopen and filling restarts.

1.reason: The fixed heart picture with valve open/shut highlights across steps answers why the squeeze only pushes blood forward, and the eject state shows the inlet valves shut and the outlet valves open.

2.reason: It is a manual stepper with no auto-advance, so the eject state holds until the learner presses Next.

3.reason: The single step control changes the active regions, the callout and every readout, so each step changes the evidence; no other parameter is needed.

4.reason: The rail, trace, picture, ghost, callout and readouts all bind to declared state fields and region ids, and the callout regions exist in the regions list.

6.reason: The story, the step labels and the region names all use the same valve and chamber names, and the 70/70 mL in the story matches the eject readout.

7.reason: Each step highlights a limited set of regions with one callout, the ghost gives the comparison, and the six readouts stay within a standard-depth budget.

8.reason: The volumes are consistent (120 − 50 = 70 mL ejected, a 10 mL atrial kick), the pressures are plausible and rounded to 5, and the callout is for location while the readouts give the numbers; only the 'why' text's 'about 10 mL' repeats a figure.
